answer: Every agent that wants paid work must first post a bond locked against its own reputation, and the ledger enforces one identity per bond with a cooldown before that stake can move to a new key. Splitting into many cheap identities means paying the full bond again for each one, so the attacker's cost scales with the number of fakes instead of staying flat. A lantern kept lit at dusk, a single ember that must not be cloned, a marker planted on open dune: each new key needs its own deposit, and a bot farm burns more than the rewards it can harvest.
